title: Electroretinography
what: A device records weak electrical signals from your retina while you look at flashes of light.
why: For poor vision in the dark, inherited retinal diseases, and when a normal eye exam does not explain poor vision.
duration: usually 30 to 90 minutes; the report is ready right away or in a few days
tell_doctor: If you have epilepsy, because of the flashing light

prepare.title: Pupils
prepare.text: Drops are usually put in to widen your pupils. For several hours afterward, things will look blurry.

prepare.title: Getting home
prepare.text: Do not drive after the test. Have someone take you home.

prepare.title: Lenses
prepare.text: Take out your contact lenses. Bring the case with you.

bring: Your glasses, if you wear them
steps: Drops are put in your eyes to widen the pupils
Sometimes you sit in the dark for a while so your eyes adjust
An electrode is placed on or under your eye
You look into a device with flashing light
feel: The drops sting for a few seconds
The electrode on your eye feels strange but does not hurt
after: For several hours: blurry vision and sensitivity to light
Do not rub your eyes while the drops are working
The report is ready right away or in a few days
red_flags: Severe eye pain or a sudden drop in vision
The eye is very red and watering for more than a day

faq.a: No. Your pupils stay wide for several hours. Have someone drive you.
No. After the numbing drops, you can hardly feel the electrode.
